scope: Two familiar registered training families; four fresh attempts per arm
diagnosis: Both candidate recursive first responses requested delegation as bare Python calls, without executable REPL fences. The pinned parser executed neither. Both then repaired directly; one completed a tested repair, while the other corrected source on its last local turn but returned an invalid final patch and remained failed.
ordinary_prompt_divergence: Both initial ordinary requested and effective prompts match the preserved prior protocol. One BASE first output differs immediately despite that equality, losing its historical tested pass. The cause is unresolved; no causal attribution to the recursive role change is established.
limitations: Familiar training-family results do not establish generalization or combined recursive improvement.
A three-gain/one-loss net increase does not satisfy the no-individual-loss gate.
All historical comparisons are descriptive only. Fresh BASE outputs were used in this comparison.
Output token IDs and complete trajectories were not replayed; exact recorded check scripts and canonical prompt/context/output counts were verified.
